human_tolerance.notes: The article lists gardens first among the habitats where the species is common, alongside fynbos, forests and coastal scrub.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds from April to December depending on region; the closed oval nest has a side entrance, sometimes with a porch.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Mainly resident, so the non-breeding part of the year is held on territory; birds in the north-east of the range are partially migratory.

vocalizations.description: A high-pitched jumble of tinkling notes rising and falling in pitch and tempo for three to five seconds or more.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 7340753 from the species/match endpoint and iNaturalist taxon 145157 from the taxa endpoint; the Wikidata QID is the one the English article's taxobox links to.

conservation.note: The species article's taxobox records IUCN category Least Concern.

range.note: The article says only that the species 'breeds in southern Africa', with no country list. South Africa alone is recorded rather than inventing a country set the source does not give; the locale this record was written for is in South Africa. Koppen classes reflect the winter-rainfall fynbos and montane forest the habitat sentence names.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Flight is fast and direct on short wings' and 'It can take nectar by hovering like a hummingbird', which between them give Fly and Hover.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The closed oval nest is constructed from grass, lichen and other plant material, bound together with spider webs', with a side entrance.

traits.perching.note: 'It usually perches to feed most of the time'.

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 7.73 g for Cinnyris chalybeus, sourced by AVONET to Dunning.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Authored bracket of 6.5-9 g around the AVONET mean. No sourced range for this species was found; treat as an estimate.

traits.length_m.note: 'The southern double-collared sunbird is 12 cm long'.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Twice the AVONET Wing.Length of 52 mm, rounded to 0.104 m. AVONET does not give a wingspan directly.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Honest gap. Neither the species article, Wikidata nor GBIF gives a longevity figure for this species, and no openly licensed source with one was found. 5 years is an authored placeholder for a small passerine; it is not a sourced value.

traits.diet.note: 'It lives mainly on nectar from flowers, but takes some fruit, and, especially when feeding young, insects and spiders.' The 0.55/0.3/0.15 split is authored from that ordering; the source gives no proportions.

traits.senses.note: Authored: diurnal nectar-feeding passerine with coloured vision and modest olfaction.

traits.social.note: 'Usually seen singly or in small groups'; the upper bound of 5 is authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Recorded as diurnal: an active daytime bird with no nocturnal behaviour described.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from a bird described as 'common in gardens', where people are routine.

habitat.use.note: AVONET classifies the habitat as Shrubland with an insessorial lifestyle, which matches the article's fynbos, forest and coastal scrub. The 0.85 arboreal / 0.15 aerial split reflects a bird that perches to feed and only occasionally hovers; it is authored.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts in dense woody cover.

habitat.resources.note: Food tags follow the diet sentence in the article; perch follows 'usually perches to feed', and the nest follows the nest description. Weights are authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'Common in gardens' is sourced; urban_affinity and light_max are authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It is mainly resident, but partially migratory in the north-east of its range' - no migration is described for the Western Cape, so ActiveYearRound is recorded rather than a migration strategy that does not apply here.

seasonal.phases.note: The April to December breeding season is stated; the non-breeding window and its 'territorial' label are authored.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Authored: a small passerine that builds a suspended cup nest and fledges in about six weeks. The source gives no incubation or nestling period.

vocalizations.song.note: 'The song is high pitched jumble of tinkling notes, rising and falling in pitch and tempo for 3-5 seconds or more.'

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'The call is a hard chee-chee', given as a separate call from the song in the source.

look.note: Adult male glossy metallic green head, throat, upper breast and back, with a brilliant red chest band separated from the green breast by a narrow metallic blue band and whitish remaining underparts; black bill, legs and feet, dark brown eye, and yellow shoulder tufts visible in display. Proportions, including the long decurved bill, are authored.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: a perch-and-glean nectar feeder that perches to feed, hovers occasionally, and suspends a cup nest between April and December.
